messages.content: "Imagine you are a drone operator. You are currently operating a drone that is at a point (5, 7) in the sky. You are asked to move the drone to a new point (10, 15). After reaching the new point, you are again asked to move the drone to another point (20, 25). Can you calculate the total distance the drone has traveled using the Euclidean norm method?"

function.name: math_hypot
function.description: Calculate the Euclidean norm, sqrt(sum(squares)), the length of the vector from the origin to point (x, y) which is the hypotenuse of the right triangle. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

z.description: Optional. The z-coordinate value. Default is 0.

message.reasoning: We need to calculate total distance traveled by drone moving from (5,7) to (10,15), then from (10,15) to (20,25). Use Euclidean norm (hypotenuse). We can use the provided function math_hypot. We'll call it twice: first for displacement between (5,7) and (10,15). That displacement vector is (10-5, 15-7) = (5,8). So distance1 = sqrt(5^2 + 8^2) = sqrt(25+64)=sqrt(89). Then second displacement between (10,15) and (20,25): vector (10,10). Distance2 = sqrt(10^2 + 10^2) = sqrt(200). Total distance = sqrt(89)+sqrt(200). We can compute numeric approximations: sqrt(89) ≈ 9.433... sqrt(200) ≈ 14.142... sum ≈ 23.575... But we might want to keep exact form: sqrt(89)+sqrt(200). sqrt(200)=10*sqrt(2). So total = sqrt(89)+10*sqrt(2). Provide answer. Use function calls.
